newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish banks expect tame growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Spanish banks expect tame growth in 1997.

text.p: Spanish banks should see another year of tame profit growth in 1997 as net interest income slips and financial trading income rises, private banking association chairman Jose Luis Leal said on Wednesday.
"We'll have a very similar year to last year," Leal told reporters at a new conference.
In 1996, overall net profit rose 3.9 percent to 399 billion pesetas, making the year "not very good," Leal said.
A likely recovery in economic growth and a possible increase in efficiency should compensate falling interest income due to the decline in market yields and in official rates.
Return on assets in 1996 was 8.23 percent versus to 8.90 percent in 1995, while the average cost of liabilities was 1.98 percent versus 2.2 percent.
He also said that the making of the European single currency should boost deals between commercial banks of different countries.
